samples.summary: New spill cleanup copies only half of `removeData`'s spill contract — blocked anchors are never re-queued
samples.evidence: The delta clears spill anchors/ghosts under a moved merge (sheet.ts:2396-2415) and explicitly claims it follows "the same cleanup contract `removeData` follows". But `removeData` (sheet.ts:1117-1166) has a second half: for every cell it clears it calls `consumeSpillBlocker(sref)` and feeds the resulting `unblockedAnchors` back into `changedSrefs`/`dependantsMap` so a spill that was blocked by that cell can re-attempt. `moveRangeTo` never calls `consumeSpillBlocker` at all (only call sites are setData:1082 and removeData:1151), so a destination cell that was blocking a spill and is now cleared leaves the blocked anchor stuck in `#SPILL!` state. The contract the comment invokes is only partially implemented.

samples.evidence: sheet.ts:2396-2420 is a near-literal copy of sheet.ts:1119-1147 (ghost skip, `spillRows && spillCols && !spillBlocked` anchor teardown loop, `else if (cell.spillBlocked)` branch, style-preserving set/delete). The repo's convention is reuse; a `clearCellPreservingStyle(ref, cell)` helper on `Sheet` would keep the two call sites from drifting — which they already have (see the missing `consumeSpillBlocker` step).

samples.summary: Drag-move section of the sheets design doc does not record the newly added covered-cell clearing / spill teardown semantics
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:112-119 describes merge propagation for drag-move (moved merge re-created, fully covered merge dropped, partial overlap rejected) but says nothing about the behaviour this PR adds: destination cells covered by the re-created merge are cleared (including tearing down spill anchors and their ghosts) and merge-alias invalidation forces recalculation of dependants of dropped merges. These are user-visible data-loss-adjacent semantics that belong in the canonical subsystem doc rather than only in code comments.

finding.summary: New spill cleanup copies only half of `removeData`'s spill contract — blocked anchors are never re-queued
finding.evidence: The delta clears spill anchors/ghosts under a moved merge (sheet.ts:2396-2415) and explicitly claims it follows "the same cleanup contract `removeData` follows". But `removeData` (sheet.ts:1117-1166) has a second half: for every cell it clears it calls `consumeSpillBlocker(sref)` and feeds the resulting `unblockedAnchors` back into `changedSrefs`/`dependantsMap` so a spill that was blocked by that cell can re-attempt. `moveRangeTo` never calls `consumeSpillBlocker` at all (only call sites are setData:1082 and removeData:1151), so a destination cell that was blocking a spill and is now cleared leaves the blocked anchor stuck in `#SPILL!` state. The contract the comment invokes is only partially implemented.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `consumeSpillBlocker` (sheet.ts:977-981) has only two call sites in the entire repo — setData (1082) and removeData (1151) — per a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `spillBlocker`. removeData implements both halves of the contract: it clears ghosts/registrations AND collects `unblockedAnchors` (1115, 1151-1152) to re-queue them into changedSrefs/dependantsMap before `calculate` (1162-1166). The new moveRangeTo destination-clear block (2389-2421) explicitly invokes "the same cleanup contract `removeData` follows" (2398-2399) but only calls `clearSpillBlockers` (2401, 2414); it never consumes the blocker registration for the cell it clears, and neither does any other part of moveRangeTo (setGrid 2323, source clear 2346-2356). I also checked for an indirect re-queue: calculate() (calculator.ts:41-166) only registers (117) / clears (130) blockers and has no blocked-anchor rescan, and a blocked anchor only reaches dependantsMap if the blocking cell is one of its formula references, which is not generally true (e.g. =SEQUENCE(3) blocked by a literal). So a previously-blocking destination cell that the merge propagation clears leaves its anchor stuck in the blocked #REF!/#SPILL! state. Under the design-fit lane this is a duplication/reuse fit violation: the spill-cleanup block is copy-pasted a third time (setData 1046-1065, removeData 1126-1140, moveRangeTo 2400-2415) rather than extracted into a shared helper, and the newest copy silently implements only part of the contract it names. Note the issue doc's acceptance criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheet-move-merge-propagation-todo.md:43-54) say nothing about spill state, so this is not a missed acceptance criterion per se — it is the duplication/incomplete-invariant strand of the lane. No counterexample found, so the finding stays.
